title: Comparable: Semantic Versions

docs.title: Protocols — Adopting a Protocol Using a Synthesized Implementation

hints: Implement `<` (and `==` where needed) to conform to `Comparable`.
Parse into three integers padded with zeros; compare them lexicographically. Exclude the original text from equality.
jsBridge: Conforming to `Comparable` means implementing `<`. You get `>`, `<=`, `sorted()`, `max()` and `clamped` for free. JS needs a comparator function passed everywhere, while Swift puts ordering on the type.

compass.q: semver comparison in JS needs a library call each time. What does putting `<` on the type let every API use automatically?
Must `"2" == "2.0.0"`? If `==` says yes but the hash differs, what breaks in a `Set<Version>`?
`Comparable` conformance vs `sorted(by:)` closures: when does the type have a *natural* order?
App version checks ("force update below 2.3"): where does this logic live, and how do you get the app's version?
